chunk_reasons: Source p_00126, “Understanding when balances are reported to credit bureaus.” This adds the missing mechanism: card balances are typically reported monthly, usually on or around the statement closing date, which is the last day of the billing cycle, not the payment due date. This is necessary because the primary says to pay by the end of the billing cycle, but only this chunk explains why that timing matters for what gets reflected in utilization reporting.

Source p_00155 / p_00146, explaining that cash advances generally have no grace period and interest begins accruing the same day. This adds a different necessary consequence not contained in the primary: even if paying before the billing-cycle end may help limit utilization impact, the borrower may still incur immediate interest costs. This depends on the primary because the “no grace period” fact matters specifically in the context of cash advances, not ordinary purchases.
